modules.name: RaffleFactory
modules.role: Ownerless factory with no admin, pause, upgrade or rescue. The constructor fixes quoteToken (checked only for code and decimals()==6), vrfWrapper (checked only for code) and protocolTreasury (screened against self, quote, wrapper and implementation), then deploys the single Raffle implementation, whose constructor captures factory=msg.sender. createRaffle validates the sponsor's params, ERC-1167-clones the implementation (CREATE) and initializes the clone. It then writes the raffleById/idByRaffle/isRaffle registry and pulls the prize with prize.safeTransferFrom(sponsor, clone, id), verifying prize.ownerOf==clone and clone.status()==Active. Every clone reads the registry (isRaffle, raffleImplementation) to screen destinations.

modules.name: Raffle
modules.role: Per-raffle ERC-1167 clone (614 lines). It combines four things. (1) Escrow of one prize NFT. (2) USDC accounting in five buckets: unsettledPot, remainingRefundLiability, winnerProceeds, sponsorProceeds and protocolFees. (3) The 'raffle.fun Ticket' ERC-721, with one sequential ticket per purchase holding an inclusive uint128 entry range. (4) A Chainlink VRF v2.5 native-payment wrapper consumer. Lifecycle: AwaitingPrize -> Active -> Drawing -> NftWon|CashWon, plus Active|Drawing -> Refunding on timeouts. The constructor locks the implementation's own storage (initialized=true, status=Refunding). User-facing mutators are nonReentrant, except initialize, onERC721Received, inherited rawFulfillRandomWords and the inherited ERC721 transfer/approval functions. Unrelated NFTs sent with plain transferFrom stay stuck by design (documented). USDC accounting uses nominal amounts with no balance-delta checks.

modules.name: IRaffle
modules.role: Raffle ABI: Status enum, RaffleInitParams struct, events, custom errors and NatSpec pre/postconditions. No logic. The NatSpec states trust assumptions: the quote token is canonical USDC with standard, non-rebasing, fee-free transfers, and 'Supported prizes are honest, standards-compliant ERC-721s'. This differs from DESIGN.md, which treats arbitrary prize contracts as untrusted.

modules.name: IRaffleFactory
modules.role: Factory ABI: CreateRaffleParams (sponsorRecipient, prizeToken, prizeTokenId, reserveEntries, endTime), RaffleCreated event, errors, and the registry/config getters that clones call during screening. No logic. The NatSpec says deployment tooling must verify the canonical USDC address because on-chain checks are limited to code and decimals.

modules.name: RaffleConstants
modules.role: Fixed v1 economics, timing and limits: BPS=10_000, PROTOCOL_FEE_BPS=500, CASH_WINNER_BPS=8000, ENTRY_PRICE=1_000_000, QUOTE_TOKEN_DECIMALS=6, MAX_REFUND_TICKET_BATCH_SIZE=100, MAX_SALE_DURATION=30 days, DRAW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=2 days, DRAW_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT=2 days, VRF_CALLBACK_GAS_LIMIT=300_000, VRF_REQUEST_CONFIRMATIONS=30. Because gross is always a multiple of 1e6, the 5% and 80% mulDiv results come out exact.

modules.name: Inherited OpenZeppelin 5.6.1 (ERC721, ERC721Utils, ReentrancyGuard, SafeERC20, Math, Clones)
modules.role: Not in src, but part of the deployed ABI and behavior. ERC721 provides public transferFrom, safeTransferFrom (two overloads), approve and setApprovalForAll with no reentrancy guard; all ticket mints, transfers and burns go through the Raffle._update override. _safeMint and safeTransferFrom call the recipient's onERC721Received. ReentrancyGuard is storage-based at the ERC-7201 slot 0x9b779b17...5f00. Fresh clones hold 0 there, which counts as not-entered because the check is ==ENTERED(2). Math.mulDiv rounds down. Clones.clone uses CREATE.

modules.name: Inherited Chainlink VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase (@chainlink/contracts 1.5.0)
modules.role: Provides the immutables i_vrfV2PlusWrapper and i_linkToken (its constructor calls wrapper.link()). It also provides external rawFulfillRandomWords, whose only authentication is msg.sender==wrapper before dispatching to Raffle.fulfillRandomWords; it has no reentrancy guard. Its internal requestRandomnessPayInNative re-quotes calculateRequestPriceNative and forwards exactly that value. It also exposes the getBalance and getLinkToken views.

entrypoints.name: RaffleFactory.createRaffle(CreateRaffleParams)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Any EOA or contract. msg.sender becomes the sponsor and must own params.prizeTokenId and have approved the factory as operator. nonReentrant. Calls into the sponsor-chosen prize contract (supportsInterface, safeTransferFrom, ownerOf).

entrypoints.name: Raffle.initialize(RaffleInitParams)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Only the immutable factory, exactly once, atomically inside createRaffle. Always reverts on the implementation instance.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.onERC721Received(operator, from, tokenId, data)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone can call it. It succeeds only while AwaitingPrize, with msg.sender == configured prizeToken, tokenId == prizeTokenId, from == sponsor and operator == factory. Normally reached through prize.safeTransferFrom inside createRaffle. No reentrancy guard.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.buyEntries(recipient, entryCount)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Any payer (msg.sender, needs a USDC allowance) while Active and block.timestamp < endTime. The recipient can be any non-protocol address and gets an onERC721Received callback if it has code.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.requestDraw() payable
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone while Active with totalEntries > 0 and endTime <= block.timestamp < endTime + 2 days. The caller pays the native VRF fee and gets the excess back through a full-gas low-level call.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.rawFulfillRandomWords(requestId, randomWords) [inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase]
entrypoints.reachableBy: Only the immutable Chainlink VRF v2.5 wrapper (msg.sender check). Dispatches to internal Raffle.fulfillRandomWords. No reentrancy guard.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.enableRefunds()
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone once the applicable deadline is reached: endTime if Active with no entries, endTime + 2 days if sold and not drawn, drawRequestedAt + 2 days if Drawing. The sponsor address (not sponsorRecipient) may call it at any time while Active with zero entries.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.settleWinningTicket(ticketId)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone, once, while NftWon or CashWon. The caller supplies the ticket ID whose range must contain winningEntry. Ticket ownership is not read.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.redeemWinningTicket(ticketId)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Only the current ownerOf the winning ticket (approved operators cannot), once, while NftWon or CashWon. Settles inline if settlement has not happened yet.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.refundTickets(uint256[] ticketIds)
entrypoints.reachableBy: Ticket owners while Refunding. 1 to 100 IDs per call, each owned by msg.sender (operators cannot refund).

entrypoints.name: Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds()
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone. Pays the immutable sponsorRecipient when sponsorProceeds > 0.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.releaseProtocolFees()
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone. Pays the immutable protocolTreasury when protocolFees > 0.

entrypoints.name: Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize()
entrypoints.reachableBy: Anyone while CashWon or Refunding and the prize is not yet claimed. Sends the NFT to the immutable sponsorRecipient.

entrypoints.name: Raffle ticket ERC-721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (2 overloads) / approve / setApprovalForAll [inherited OZ ERC721]

actors.name: Factory deployer: chooses quoteToken, vrfWrapper and protocolTreasury once; no powers after deployment
RaffleFactory contract: sole clone initializer, prize-deposit operator, isRaffle registry source
Chainlink VRF v2.5 native wrapper and its coordinator/oracles: price quotes, request IDs, randomness callback
Quote token, canonical 6-decimal USDC: assumed standard, non-rebasing and fee-free; issuer-side controls are outside the system
Protocol treasury: immutable, passive fee recipient
Sponsor (createRaffle msg.sender): picks prizeToken, prizeTokenId, sponsorRecipient, reserveEntries and endTime within factory bounds; can call enableRefunds early only while zero entries are sold
Sponsor recipient: sponsor-chosen address that receives sponsor USDC and the returned prize NFT

Prize ERC-721 contract: arbitrary sponsor-chosen code called at creation, redemption and prize return; it is the msg.sender authenticating onERC721Received and it answers its own ownerOf escrow and delivery checks. DESIGN.md says untrusted; IRaffle NatSpec assumes 'honest, standards-compliant'
Ticket holder: bearer of a transferable range ticket; ownerOf at call time decides refund and redemption rights
Ticket recipient contracts: get onERC721Received callbacks from _safeMint and ticket safeTransferFrom
Approved ticket operators: can move tickets but cannot refund or redeem
Draw requester: anyone who funds requestDraw; receives excess native value through a full-gas call
Permissionless keepers calling enableRefunds, settleWinningTicket, releaseSponsorProceeds, releaseProtocolFees, releaseSponsorPrize
Frontends and indexers: advisory discovery only; transactions must reread chain state

state.name: status: lifecycle enum. AwaitingPrize -> Active -> Drawing -> NftWon|CashWon, or Active|Drawing -> Refunding. NftWon, CashWon and Refunding are terminal; the implementation is fixed at Refunding; a fresh clone's zero value is AwaitingPrize
initialized: one-shot initialization lock
Write-once per-raffle config: sponsor, sponsorRecipient, protocolTreasury, prizeToken, prizeTokenId, raffleId, reserveEntries, endTime
totalEntries, ticketCount: uint128 sale counters; totalEntries is frozen once block.timestamp >= endTime
_ticketRanges[ticketId]: inclusive [firstEntry,lastEntry]. Assumed contiguous and disjoint, covering exactly [1,totalEntries]; kept after burn
ERC-721 ticket ledger (_owners, _balances, _tokenApprovals, _operatorApprovals); ownerOf gates refunds and redemption
unsettledPot: gross USDC held before a terminal state; equals totalEntries*ENTRY_PRICE while Active or Drawing
remainingRefundLiability: set once from unsettledPot on entering Refunding, then reduced per refund with checked subtraction
winnerProceeds: CashWon 80% allocation (rounded down), zeroed on redemption
sponsorProceeds: remainder allocation (95% on NftWon, 15% on CashWon), zeroed on release
protocolFees: 5% allocation (rounded down), zeroed on release
vrfRequestId, drawRequestedAt: ID and timestamp of the single accepted VRF request; drawRequestedAt anchors callbackDeadline
_requestInFlight: true only during the wrapper request call, so a synchronous callback is ignored
winningEntry, resolvedAt: selected entry in [1,totalEntries] and the resolution timestamp
settlementComplete, winningTicketId: one-shot settlement record
winnerRedeemed, winnerRecipient: one-shot redemption record
prizeClaimed: one release flag shared by winner NFT delivery and the sponsor prize return
ReentrancyGuard slot 0x9b779b17...5f00, per clone; 0 in a fresh clone counts as not-entered
Immutables in the implementation code, shared by every clone: factory, quoteToken, i_vrfV2PlusWrapper, i_linkToken

Clone USDC balance (held in the quoteToken contract): expected to be >= accountedQuoteBalance() = unsettledPot + remainingRefundLiability + winnerProceeds + sponsorProceeds + protocolFees. Not checked on-chain; unsolicited transfers go unaccounted
Prize NFT custody (held in the prizeToken contract): prizeToken.ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == clone between escrow and release
Clone native balance: only transient, inside requestDraw (receive reverts)
raffleCount: lifetime raffle ID counter, starting at 1
Registry raffleById / idByRaffle / isRaffle: written after initialize and before prize escrow; every clone checks isRaffle when screening destinations
Factory immutables: quoteToken, vrfWrapper, protocolTreasury, raffleImplementation

candidates.name: Raffle.redeemWinningTicket (L309-346)
candidates.why: Only path that delivers the main prize. Checks winnerRedeemed and NftWon/CashWon, settles inline or requires ticketId==winningTicketId, requires ownerOf==msg.sender, records the winner and burns, then sends the NFT (untrusted prizeToken.transferFrom + ownerOf check) or the cash (_transferQuote). The design requires every effect to revert if delivery fails.

candidates.name: Raffle._settleWinningTicket (L533-558), reached via settleWinningTicket L304 and redeemWinningTicket
candidates.why: Permissionless, one-shot split of the whole unsettledPot into protocolFees (5%, rounded down), winnerProceeds (80%, rounded down, CashWon only) and sponsorProceeds (the remainder); sets settlementComplete/winningTicketId and zeroes the pot. Conservation and the 95/5 vs 80/15/5 splits depend on this function.

candidates.name: Raffle.buyEntries (L209-237)
candidates.why: Only USDC inflow and only ticket mint. Checks status, time, recipient, count>0 and uint128 headroom; credits the nominal amount with no balance-delta check (fee-free token assumption); assigns the next contiguous range and bumps the counters and unsettledPot; then _safeMint calls the untrusted recipient. The range-partition invariant starts here.

candidates.name: Raffle.refundTickets (L349-372)
candidates.why: Untrusted array of 1-100 IDs during Refunding. Per ID: owner check (ownerOf reverts on burned or nonexistent tickets, which also rejects duplicates), range sum, burn. The total is debited from remainingRefundLiability (checked) and paid to msg.sender. Conservation assumes the ranges partition [1,totalEntries].

candidates.name: Raffle.enableRefunds (L276-301)
candidates.why: Terminal move to Refunding with three deadline cases (empty Active: sponsor any time, others at endTime; sold Active: endTime+2d; Drawing: drawRequestedAt+2d) that moves unsettledPot into remainingRefundLiability. These >= boundaries must not overlap the < windows of buyEntries, requestDraw and callback acceptance.

candidates.name: Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (L509-524), reached via inherited rawFulfillRandomWords
candidates.why: Decides the winner and outcome. Silently ignores in-flight, non-Drawing, wrong-ID, wrong-length or late callbacks; otherwise sets winningEntry = word % totalEntries + 1 and status NftWon if totalEntries >= reserveEntries, else CashWon. Relies on totalEntries being frozen after endTime and on wrapper authentication.

candidates.name: Raffle.requestDraw (L240-273)
candidates.why: Payable, permissionless move from Active to Drawing in [endTime, endTime+2d) when totalEntries>0. Checks msg.value against the quote; sets status, drawRequestedAt and _requestInFlight before the trusted wrapper call; records vrfRequestId; then refunds msg.value-paidPrice to msg.sender through a full-gas low-level call while the guard is held.

candidates.name: RaffleFactory.createRaffle (L97-148)

Escrow is verified by prize.ownerOf==clone and status()==Active, and both checks depend on how the prize contract behaves.

candidates.name: Raffle.onERC721Received (L416-431)

invariants.claim: For a non-sponsor caller, an empty Active raffle can be closed from t >= endTime. This is the exact complement of the buyEntries window t < endTime; at t == endTime, buyEntries reverts and this call passes.

A sold Active raffle can be closed from t >= endTime + 2 days. This is the exact complement of the requestDraw window t < drawRequestDeadline(). Both sides call the same function, and endTime is written only once.

A Drawing raffle can be closed from t >= drawRequestedAt + 2 days. This is the exact complement of callback acceptance (t < callbackDeadline()). Both sides call the same function, so same-block ordering cannot matter at the boundary.

The sponsor's untimed path overlaps the buyEntries window in time but is excluded by state. The path needs totalEntries == 0 at execution, buyEntries needs Active, and totalEntries only increases (sole writer, entryCount > 0). After any purchase, later calls take the endTime + 2 days branch.
The entire unsettledPot moves into remainingRefundLiability, so accountedQuoteBalance() is the same before and after the call.
On the empty-raffle branch, the liability moved is 0 and no tickets exist.
The body makes no external call. The guard is the only modifier, and the three storage writes and the event happen with no observable intermediate state.

Every non-terminal state after escrow has a finite time from which any caller passes: endTime when empty, endTime + 2 days when sold, and drawRequestedAt + 2 days when Drawing. Because drawRequestedAt lies in [endTime, endTime + 2 days), the Drawing deadline is below endTime + 4 days.

trustBoundaries.actor: Anyone (deployers of third-party proxies, direct callers of the implementation)
trustBoundaries.reaches: The implementation is locked (Refunding, initialized) and every mutator reverts; setApprovalForAll writes only to its own storage. Third-party proxies can never be initialized (L178), stay AwaitingPrize with prizeToken 0, are not registered and are not denylist members.

See flags and events that can come before custody or differ from final ownership: isRaffle true during W1, TicketPurchased before RaffleCreated, TicketPurchased.recipient different from the owner, prizeClaimed/winnerRedeemed true before delivery, and RaffleResolved before DrawRequested if a callback lands in W5.

fragilityClusters.area: Prize custody self-reported by the prize contract: RaffleFactory.createRaffle RF L127-L134, Raffle.onERC721Received L416-L431, redeemWinningTicket L329-L337, releaseSponsorPrize L395-L407
fragilityClusters.why: The sponsor-chosen contract answers every custody check: escrow acceptance (arguments it supplies), the escrow check (RF L129) and both delivery checks (L335, L405). Nothing observes custody independently. IRaffle NatSpec (honest prizes) and DESIGN.md (untrusted prizes) disagree. In NftWon, one external transferFrom is the only NFT exit, while the sponsor's 95% and the treasury's 5% are released independently.

Between Raffle L428 (Active) and RF L129-L132, the new clone is already registered (isRaffle true) and Active, with its guard open, while sponsor-chosen code runs. buyEntries, ticket transfers and approvals, and a sponsor-driven enableRefunds are reachable. RF L132 checks only status, so purchases survive, and TicketPurchased logs come before RaffleCreated.

fragilityClusters.area: Point-in-time destination screening: Raffle._isProtocolDestination L593-L605 with callers L187-L195, L498, L565; unscreened outflows L334, L404, L267 and approvals
fragilityClusters.why: Each outflow is screened at a different moment. The result can flip from false to true only for code-less future CREATE addresses, which are computable because raffleById[k] = CREATE(factory, k+1). The screen covers only same-factory plumbing (not LINK, the coordinator, other factories' clones, third-party proxies, or other raffles' prizes). USDC to sponsorRecipient is screened again at release, but the NFT is not. A treasury equal to a future clone address halts creation at that nonce permanently.

fragilityClusters.area: VRF request/callback boundary: requestDraw L240-L273, fulfillRandomWords L509-L524, VCB L76-L107
fragilityClusters.why: _requestInFlight covers only the wrapper call (W4). The full-gas native refund to msg.sender (W5) runs after status=Drawing and vrfRequestId are set. It is the one point where Raffle code does not exclude an unguarded state writer (rawFulfillRandomWords) running inside a guarded frame. Request-ID semantics, routing, re-delivery, gas forwarding, value returned by the wrapper, configuration bounds and caller-chosen gas price all depend on wrapper code that is not vendored. Time boundaries at L512/L291 are exact complements.

fragilityClusters.area: Terminal-state claim decoupling: settleWinningTicket/_settleWinningTicket L304-L306/L533-L558, redeemWinningTicket L309-L346, releaseSponsorProceeds L375-L382, releaseProtocolFees L385-L392, releaseSponsorPrize L395-L407
fragilityClusters.why: Settlement is permissionless and touches only storage, so sponsor and treasury USDC become releasable whether or not the winner's delivery succeeds. Redemption is a bearer claim with no deadline and no alternative claimant: one NFT exit in NftWon, one consumer of winnerProceeds in CashWon. One-shot flags shared across functions are separated only by status, and they read true before the prize contract runs.

fragilityClusters.area: Nominal USDC accounting: buyEntries L223-L233, enableRefunds L296-L298, refundTickets L363-L369, _settleWinningTicket L539-L555, _transferQuote L564-L567
fragilityClusters.why: Every amount is ENTRY_PRICE × entries, and src never reads balanceOf. Solvency rests on USDC being fee-free and non-rebasing, and on issuer controls (pause, blocklist) not applying. Those controls can block fixed payees or holders. Unclaimed liabilities and unsolicited surplus have no sweep and no deadline.

fragilityClusters.area: Unguarded ERC-721 ticket surface and receiver callbacks: E L93-L136 via Raffle._update L497-L502; mint hook R L235 → E L289
fragilityClusters.why: Tickets move in every lifecycle status; there is no status gate. Hooks from top-level safeTransferFrom run with the clone guard not entered, so a new owner can refund or redeem inside the callback. Operator approvals persist per owner. Raffle reads ownership only at L320 and L359, each followed immediately by a burn. TicketPurchased.recipient can differ from the owner when the call returns.

fragilityClusters.area: Timeline hand-offs and keeper dependence: buyEntries L216, requestDraw L242-L247, enableRefunds L276-L301, drawRequestDeadline/callbackDeadline L458-L465, fulfillRandomWords L512
fragilityClusters.why: Each of three hand-offs uses one deadline function on both sides. The sponsor's untimed exit for a raffle with no sales overlaps the sale window and is separated only by state. Nothing transitions automatically and there is no incentive to call, so refunds and the prize return wait for someone to call enableRefunds. Terminal states have no deadlines. Block-producer timestamps decide which side a boundary block lands on.

fragilityClusters.area: Creation-time validation split between RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams RF L154-L179 and Raffle.initialize L176-L206
fragilityClusters.why: Different checks live in different contracts: the sponsor checks, treasury-vs-prize, recipient-vs-new-clone, and the code-gated isRaffle query are in initialize only. Admission accepts raffle tickets from other factory deployments as prizes, since it excludes only same-factory clones. reserveEntries has no upper bound. The clone stores the factory-validated parameters without rechecking them.
